A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UDS research work. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original fine-tuning accuracy, throughput, correlation analyses, ablations, and robustness experiments in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds larger-model, longer-context, selection-behavior, and computational-efficiency results.

M1.justification: UDS retains the same nuclear-norm scoring, bilinear projection, FIFO memory buffer, combined importance score, and top-K selection procedure. Algorithm 1 and the method equations are unchanged.

E1.justification: The datasets and task coverage remain unchanged, including MATH long-context reasoning and MATH500/AMC23 OOD evaluation. The additional sequence-length budget and 14B backbone extend experimental settings within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: The online comparator set is retained, and FisherSFT already appears in v3 Table 15. v4 Table 17 preserves its accuracy results; the newly documented projection does not establish that the comparator implementation changed between versions.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds Qwen-2.5-14B full-parameter fine-tuning and a 32768-token MATH setting alongside the retained 2048-token setting. New evaluation designs measure stage-specific FLOPs, selection-only time, peak GPU memory, and selected versus non-selected sample categories defined using initial/final median losses.

E4.justification: v4 adds substantive diagnostics of selection behavior and computational overhead: a selected/non-selected category analysis, a forward/selection/backward FLOPs breakdown, and long-context SVD timing. Larger-model and longer-window tests extend scalability analysis; the existing component, buffer, projection, and OOD analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four repetitions with different random seeds in Section 4.1 and retain the existing plus/minus reporting and correlation p-values. No new repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure is stated.

E6.justification: v4 adds 14B accuracy results and 32768-token MATH results: Table 15 reports UDS at 61.35±0.32 versus GREATS at 60.71±0.27, while retaining the 2048-token results. Tables 5, 13, 18, and 19 add FLOPs, sample-category, timing, and memory outcomes. Matched earlier accuracy entries remain unchanged; the added scores use additional settings.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, and the norm, Adam, and projection derivations in Appendix D are retained. Appendix C.4 adds an informal SVD-versus-attention scaling explanation, without a new formal guarantee or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint utility/diversity selection, avoiding external resources, and improving accuracy and training efficiency. The additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a hypothesis that redundant or stage-misaligned samples dilute useful updates. C.4 explains limited relative SVD overhead through attention scaling, and C.6 clarifies why efficiency comparisons isolate selection operations. Existing limitations remain, with sparsity-aware computation added as a future direction.

D1.justification: Appendix C.6 newly discloses FisherSFT's random projection to 1024 dimensions to avoid out-of-memory errors on a single RTX 3090, and defines the timing boundaries. This improves implementation documentation without establishing a rerun. Existing training-configuration tables and code access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references connecting online selection to RL fine-tuning, random-projection learning, data selection, and sparsity-aware computation. These broaden the surrounding context without substantially changing UDS's novelty claims or online/offline research positioning.

P1.justification: Changes include localized appendix expansions, an acknowledgment, proceedings information, and a corrected contact address. The main narrative and section hierarchy remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds appendix Tables 5, 13, 18, and 19, expands the full-fine-tuning table with a 14B block, and adds a sequence-length column and row to the MATH table. Existing figures are retained; other changes chiefly involve table relocation and page reflow.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's throughput reporting and accuracy-only FisherSFT comparison, v4 better isolates selection overhead and discloses the adapted baseline implementation, making efficiency evidence easier to assess. Larger-model and longer-window experiments provide additional scalability support. These are useful incremental gains over an already substantial empirical study; the core method, primary results, and formal support remain unchanged.
